chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Abu Basir from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:

The mukatab (slave who has contracted for manumission upon paying a sum) is not permitted to have his manumission, nor a gift, nor marriage, until he pays what is upon him. If his master stipulated to him, and he was unable, then he returns to slavery. However, he may buy and sell. And if a debt fell upon him in trade, it is upon his master to pay his debt, because he is his slave.

key_terms.اَلرِّقِّ: Slavery or state of being a slave
key_terms.اَلْمُكَاتَبُ: A slave who has contracted with his master to pay a specific sum for his freedom
key_terms.عِتْقٌ: Manumission or freeing of a slave

ai.seo_question: What are the legal restrictions and rights of a mukatab slave in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the juridical status of the *mukatab* (slave with a manumission contract), establishing that while he gains limited legal capacity to trade and own property, he remains under his master's authority until the full *kitabah* debt is paid. It highlights the principle that commercial debts incurred by the *mukatab* are borne by the master, reflecting the slave's dependent legal status, while failure to pay due to inability results in a reversion to full slavery, a key distinction in Shia fiqh regarding conditional manumission.
